results.title: GB200 NVL72 Short-Term and Reserved Capacity: Which Providers?
results.author: Colin Mo
highlights:
September 25, 2026

For short-term and reserved GB200 NVL72 capacity with managed operations, shortlist the providers whose short-term path can become the reservation without a move. AWS documents the clearest short-term form: EC2 Capacity Blocks support P6e-GB200 UltraServers and can be extended in place with the same reservation ID, but only when capacity is available, so they work best as a bridge while the reservation is negotiated separately. CoreWeave's ARENA evaluation program is built to end in a production decision, with evaluation fees credited or waived on agreed terms. GB200 NVL72 on GMI Cloud is in pre-order and coming soon, with pricing listed from $8.00 per GPU-hour on the GPU page, and our Managed GPU Cluster service, which GMI provisions and operates, is in early access on H200 nodes today. With GMI, the pre-order is where any initial phase, the reservation, and the operations scope can be covered in one capacity proposal, so they aren't negotiated twice.

Whichever provider you choose, the recommendation holds only if it will put the conversion terms in writing before the short run starts, and above all these four: the reservation continues on the same racks, network, and storage; a named date when committed pricing replaces short-term pricing; a clear exit if you decide not to reserve; and an operations scope that stays the same across both terms. If a provider can't commit to the first point, plan for a migration and a second round of validation at the start of the reservation. The rest of this guide starts from that switch: what the short run has to prove, why moving costs more than the rate change, and the six terms to get in writing.

...

1. Same racks, network, and storage. The reservation continues on the allocation used in the short phase, with the same interconnect fabric and the same storage volumes. When a provider can only commit to "equivalent" capacity, ask what equivalent means and whether it could sit in a different data center.
2. A billing cutover date. The date committed pricing takes effect, stated as a calendar date or as a rule tied to your notice. The contract should also say how any overlap is billed, so the same hours aren't charged at both rates.
3. Extension and exit. How the short phase is extended if testing runs long, how much notice the provider needs, and whether an extension depends on capacity being available. Equally important is the other direction: what happens if you decide not to reserve, including the notice period and any early-exit charges.
4. A data and checkpoint exit window. How long datasets and checkpoints remain accessible after the short phase ends without a reservation, and what storage costs during that window.
5. Minimum commitment and added capacity. The smallest reservation the provider accepts for GB200 NVL72, whether the short phase counts toward it, and how more capacity is added later: at the committed price, on the same end date, and inside the same cluster.
6. An unchanged operations scope. Managed operations belong in the conversion terms. Whatever the provider operates during the short phase, such as hardware monitoring, failed-tray replacement, firmware and driver updates, and the cluster control plane, should carry into the reservation unchanged, with the same support hours and escalation contacts. A reservation that shifts part of that work back to your team is not the environment the short run tested.

...

## Getting the conversion terms into a GB200 NVL72 pre-order on GMI Cloud

GB200 NVL72 on GMI Cloud is in pre-order and coming soon, so capacity is planned ahead rather than provisioned on the spot. That makes the pre-order conversation the place to raise the conversion terms above. Ask for the length and form of any initial phase, the billing cutover date, the allocation, the region, and the operations GMI runs in each term to be covered, and we'll work through them with you as part of the pre-order. Confirm which resources stay assigned when the pricing term changes.

Across the platform, usage-adaptive GPU pricing lets pricing follow workload maturity: teams can begin on demand and move to dedicated or committed deployments once a workload settles, rather than signing a long-term commitment too early. Today that on-demand starting point applies to H100 and H200, which are available now. For GB200 NVL72, how any initial phase is priced and when committed pricing takes over are items for the pre-order proposal. Committed usage plans carry significant discounts for sustained workloads, and our sales team can walk you through the commitment options.

1. GPU generation and real availability. A B200 quote that arrives in March does not help a March deadline. Availability labels and lead times matter more than headline prices.

results.title: GPU Clouds for B300 or NVL72 Reservations with ...
results.author: Colin Mo
highlights:

...

At GMI Cloud, our NVIDIA Blackwell lineup, including B300, GB200 NVL72, and GB300 NVL72, is in pre-order and coming soon, and the delivery window, milestones, and commitment terms are set with our sales team in the quote. As with any pre-order, the signed terms decide whether a date is a commitment, and three things show whether it will hold: specific systems allocated to your order, a site that can power and cool them, and a contract remedy if the date moves. The checks below show how to tell the difference before you sign, for any quote, ours included.

...

- Notice of slippage. The provider tells you in writing as soon as a milestone is at risk, within an agreed notice period, and gives a revised date. The earlier the notice, the more of your own schedule you can move in time.
- Substitute hardware, and the right to reject it. If the provider offers a different system, region, or configuration instead, the contract should say whether price, commitment, and acceptance criteria change. Keep the right to decline a substitute that fails your acceptance test.
- Partial first delivery. If part of the order can arrive early, state the quantity, whether it shares an NVLink domain with what follows, and the date for the rest. Each stage needs its own acceptance event and billing start.
- A term that follows the real start. The committed term should begin at acceptance, so a late delivery does not shorten the months you agreed to pay for.
- Credits or exit if the date moves. Name the remedy: service credits after a set delay, or the right to leave the commitment without penalty after a longer one. Without a remedy, a committed date behaves like a forecast.

...

On GMI Cloud, NVIDIA H100 and H200 are available now, from $2.60 and $3.20 per GPU-hour. If you plan interim work with us, raise it in the same conversation as your Blackwell pre-order: how the interim usage is priced, and where your data and checkpoints will sit when the Blackwell systems arrive.

B300 is a hardware option on Prime Inference, our reserved inference service, and it is in pre-order as well.

On-demand and committed usage are priced differently, and our sales team sets up commitment options; the GPU pricing page covers current rates. results.title: Which Providers Can Benchmark B200, B300, GB200 Before You Reserve?
results.author: Colin Mo
highlights:
September 25, 2026

Choose an inference provider that lets you run your own model and your own traffic on the exact B200, B300, or GB200 NVL72 system you plan to reserve, and that writes down how every run was configured: engine, parallelism, precision, and batching. We recommend starting with GMI Cloud's Prime Inference, because its Blackwell options cover all three platforms, open for pre-order, on dedicated, single-tenant GPUs. Our engineers tune the runtime for each model and work alongside you from prototype to production, and qualified teams can get free GPU-hour trial credits to validate performance on their own workload before committing. A result you can't reproduce on the hardware you end up paying for is not a basis for a seasonal or annual commitment. Whichever provider you test with, compare one number across platforms: cost per successful request at the same p95 latency and quality targets.

...

### Price the GPU-hours you would actually reserve

Monthly GPU cost is GPUs × hours × hourly rate. Our GPU page lists pricing from $5.00 per GPU-hour for B200 and from $8.00 per GPU-hour for GB200 NVL72; both are pre-order and coming soon, so treat these as planning inputs and take the final rate, and B300's rate, from your pre-order quote. A higher hourly rate doesn't have to mean a higher cost per request: in the DeepSeek V4 Pro example above, GB200 NVL72's listed rate is twice B200's, yet its published cost per 1M output tokens is half. Only your own test shows whether that holds for your model.

...

- Billing unit and term. Prime Inference bills per GPU-hour with no minimum contract, and reserved capacity on seasonal or annual terms comes at lower hourly rates.
- Networking and storage, which are priced separately from GPU compute.
- SLA terms. Prime Inference's uptime SLA is set by GPU series and deployment configuration, and committed SLAs vary by contract.
- Retest triggers. If the reserved allocation differs from the test hardware in GPU model, system type, interconnect, or region, rerun the steady-production and long-context scenarios on it.
- Delivery date. Blackwell on GMI Cloud is pre-order and coming soon. Put the expected delivery window for the platform you choose into the pre-order, and plan the test so it runs on the same system you will receive.
